title: See the Emerald Buddha at Wat Phra Kaew
description: The most sacred image in Thailand, carved from a single block of jade and dressed by the king three times a year. Cover knees and shoulders.

title: Watch the sunset from Wat Arun
description: A seventy-metre prang encrusted with broken Chinese porcelain, best seen from the far bank as the light goes.

title: Eat your way along a Bangkok street
description: Chinatown after dark, where the woks come out onto the pavement. Follow the queues of locals rather than the signs in English.

title: Take a longtail through the Thonburi canals
description: The city was built on canals before it was built on roads, and on the west bank most of them are still there.

title: Cycle the ruins of Ayutthaya
description: The capital sacked by the Burmese in 1767, left as brick stupas and a Buddha head grown into a fig tree.

title: Climb to Doi Suthep above Chiang Mai
description: Three hundred and six steps flanked by naga serpents, to a gold chedi that has been there since 1383.

title: Spend a day at an ethical elephant sanctuary
description: Rescued working elephants, no riding and no bathing shows. The distinction between sanctuaries here matters; check before booking.

title: See the white temple at Chiang Rai
description: A privately built temple in white and mirrored glass, still unfinished, with a bridge over a pit of reaching hands.

title: Ride the 762 curves to Pai
description: A mountain road with a counted number of bends, to a valley town of hot springs and canyon ridges in the far north-west.

title: Climb the limestone at Railay
description: Seven hundred bolted routes on overhanging limestone, on a peninsula reachable only by longtail boat.

title: Kayak the mangroves at Ao Thalane
description: Limestone karst rising straight out of mangrove channels, with the tide carrying you in and out. Quieter than Phang Nga.

title: Paddle into the hongs of Phang Nga Bay
description: Collapsed cave systems that form hidden lagoons inside the islands, entered lying flat in a kayak at low tide.

title: Sleep on a raft house at Cheow Lan Lake
description: Limestone towers out of an emerald reservoir, in a rainforest older than the Amazon. Hornbills at dawn, gibbons calling across the water.

title: Swim the Emerald Cave to Koh Muk
description: Eighty metres of swimming through a dark sea cave to a hidden beach inside a collapsed karst, with a rope to follow.

title: Cycle the Sukhothai historical park at dawn
description: The first Thai kingdom's capital, quieter and better preserved than Ayutthaya, with walking Buddhas in the lotus ponds.

title: Walk the old quarter's thirty-six streets
description: Each street was once a single guild's trade, and many still are. Crossing the road means walking slowly and not stopping.

title: Drink egg coffee in Hanoi
description: Invented in 1946 when milk was scarce: egg yolk whipped with condensed milk over strong coffee, served hot in a bowl of water.

title: Sleep on a boat in Bai Tu Long bay
description: The quieter half of Ha Long, with the same limestone towers and a fraction of the boats. Overnight is worth the extra day.

title: Be rowed through the caves at Trang An
description: Karst towers in flooded rice country, on a two-hour row through nine caves. The boatwomen row with their feet.

title: Ride the Ha Giang loop
description: Three hundred and fifty kilometres of mountain road along the Chinese border, through Hmong villages and the Ma Pi Leng pass.

title: Trek between the villages around Sapa
description: Rice terraces cut into the Hoang Lien Son mountains. Going with a local homestay host rather than a town agency changes the trip.

title: Go into the caves at Phong Nha
description: Home to Son Doong, the largest cave passage on earth. Paradise and Dark Cave are the accessible ones and are still vast.

title: Cycle the imperial citadel and tombs at Hue
description: The Nguyen capital, badly damaged in 1968 and slowly being restored, with emperors' tombs scattered along the Perfume River.

title: Ride the Hai Van Pass
description: Twenty-one kilometres over a spur of the Annamite range, with the weather often different on each side.

title: Have clothes made in Hoi An
description: A preserved trading port of Japanese, Chinese and French buildings, and several hundred tailors who will fit you in a day.

title: Canyon down the waterfalls at Da Lat
description: Abseiling into falls in the cool highlands the French built as a hill station. Choose the operator carefully; this one has a safety record.

title: Eat banh mi and pho on a Saigon street
description: The French left the baguette and the Vietnamese improved it. Pho in the south comes with a plate of herbs to add yourself.

title: Go down into the Cu Chi tunnels
description: Two hundred and fifty kilometres of hand-dug tunnel. A widened section is open to visitors and is still a tight squeeze.

title: Reach Cai Rang floating market at six
description: Wholesalers hang a sample of what they sell from a pole. By eight it is over, so the early boat is the only boat worth taking.

title: Watch the sun come up over Angkor Wat
description: The largest religious monument in the world. Buy the three-day pass; one day is not enough and the crowds thin after the first morning.

title: Find the faces at the Bayon
description: Two hundred and sixteen serene stone faces on fifty-four towers, at the centre of the walled city of Angkor Thom.

title: See the trees growing through Ta Prohm
description: Deliberately left partly unrestored, with silk-cotton roots prising the galleries apart. Go early; it is small and fills fast.

title: See the pink sandstone carving at Banteay Srei
description: Small, rose-coloured, and carved so finely it was long assumed to be the work of women. The best stonework at Angkor.

title: Visit Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek
description: A school turned interrogation centre, and the field where its prisoners were killed. Take the audio guide and take your time.

title: Stay in the Cardamom Mountains
description: One of the largest intact rainforests in Southeast Asia, with community-run camps funding the rangers who patrol it.

title: Taste Kampot pepper at a plantation
description: Protected by origin, nearly wiped out under the Khmer Rouge, and now grown again on the same red soil by the same families.

title: Watch the alms round at dawn in Luang Prabang
description: Hundreds of monks collect rice at first light. Watch from a distance and quietly, or do not watch at all.

title: Swim in the Kuang Si pools
description: Turquoise limestone terraces below a fifty-metre fall, with a bear rescue centre on the walk in.

title: Balloon over the Vang Vieng karsts
description: The tubing-and-buckets era is over; the town now sells sunrise balloon flights over limestone towers and rice fields.

title: Look for Irrawaddy dolphins at Si Phan Don
description: The Four Thousand Islands where the Mekong braids out, with a handful of critically endangered dolphins in one deep pool.

title: Walk the Plain of Jars
description: Thousands of stone jars two thousand years old, in a province that was the most heavily bombed place on earth. Stay on the marked paths.

title: Cross the Petronas skybridge
description: The tallest twin towers in the world, joined at the forty-first floor. Tickets are capped daily and released online.

title: Climb the steps at Batu Caves
description: Two hundred and seventy-two rainbow steps to a limestone cave temple, guarded by a forty-three metre gold statue and rude macaques.

title: Eat char kway teow in George Town
description: Malaysia's food capital, where Chinese, Malay and Indian cooking have been arguing productively for two centuries.

title: Walk the mossy forest in the Cameron Highlands
description: Tea plantations the British planted, and above them a cloud forest where everything is covered in moss and pitcher plants.

title: Climb Mount Kinabalu
description: Four thousand and ninety-five metres, climbed overnight to reach the granite summit plateau at sunrise. Permits are capped and book out.

title: See orangutans at Sepilok
description: A rehabilitation centre for orphaned orangutans in Borneo, with a nursery viewing platform and feeding twice a day.

title: Dive Sipadan's wall
description: An oceanic island dropping six hundred metres, with barracuda tornadoes and turtles everywhere. Only 176 permits a day.

title: See the bat exodus at Mulu
description: Three million wrinkle-lipped bats spiral out of Deer Cave each evening in a ribbon that takes an hour to pass.

title: Snorkel with turtles at the Perhentians
description: White sand and green turtles an hour off the east coast, closed by the monsoon from November to February.

title: Walk the Supertrees at Gardens by the Bay
description: Vertical gardens up to fifty metres tall that vent the conservatories and light up twice a night. The skywalk between two of them is the view.

title: Eat at a hawker centre with a Michelin star
description: Hawker culture is UNESCO listed. Chicken rice for a few dollars, and the queue tells you which stall to join.

title: Walk the Southern Ridges tree-top bridge
description: Ten kilometres of connected parks and elevated walkways across the south of the island, with the wave bridge at the high point.

title: Look for otters along the Singapore River
description: Smooth-coated otters recolonised the city after the water was cleaned up, and now have their own celebrity families.

title: Take a water taxi through Kampong Ayer
description: A village of thirteen thousand people on stilts over the river, six hundred years old and still occupied.

title: Walk the canopy at Ulu Temburong
description: Untouched Borneo rainforest reached by longboat, with an aluminium tower taking you above the canopy.

title: Island-hop the Bacuit archipelago
description: Limestone islands with hidden lagoons you swim or kayak into. Tours are lettered A to D; C has the best lagoons.

title: Dive the Japanese wrecks at Coron
description: A dozen ships sunk by a US air raid in September 1944, most of them shallow enough to see without technical gear.

title: Paddle the underground river at Puerto Princesa
description: Eight kilometres of navigable river inside a mountain. Permits are capped daily and must be arranged in advance.

title: Walk the rice terraces at Batad
description: Two thousand years of terracing carved into the Cordillera by hand, in an amphitheatre you walk down into and back out of.

title: See the Chocolate Hills and the tarsiers
description: Over a thousand grass-covered limestone mounds that go brown in the dry season, with a tarsier sanctuary nearby.

title: Canyoneer down to Kawasan Falls
description: Three hours of jumping, sliding and swimming down a limestone canyon to a turquoise waterfall.

title: Surf Cloud 9 at Siargao
description: A hollow right-hand reef break over shallow coral, with a boardwalk out to a viewing tower above it.

title: Swim with whale sharks at Donsol
description: The interaction here is regulated and the animals are wild and unfed, which is not true of every whale shark site in the country.

title: Watch the sun rise over the Bagan plain
description: More than two thousand temples across forty square kilometres, built between the eleventh and thirteenth centuries.

title: See the leg-rowing fishermen on Inle Lake
description: Intha fishermen row standing with one leg wrapped round the oar, above floating gardens anchored to the lake bed.

title: Walk the platform at Shwedagon Pagoda
description: Ninety-nine metres of gold plate and several thousand diamonds, walked barefoot, best at dusk when the lamps come on.

title: See the Golden Rock at Kyaiktiyo
description: A gilded boulder balanced on the edge of a cliff, said to be held by a single hair of the Buddha.
